text: Dolores, officially known as the Municipality of Dolores (Ilocano: Ili ti Dolores; Filipino: Bayan ng Dolores), is a municipality located in the province of Abra, Philippines. According to the 2024 census, it has a population of 11,967 people. The area was formerly named Bucao, after the first Tingguian (Itneg) chieftain who settled there prior to Spanish colonization, and was once part of the Municipality of Tayum. In 1882, Bucao was established as a separate pueblo following a recommendation by the parish priest of Tayum, Fr. Pío Mercado, and the Teniente Bazar of Bucao, Don Ignacio Eduarte. In 1885, the town was renamed Dolores in honor of its patron saint, Nuestra Señora de los Dolores (Our Lady of Sorrows). The first gobernadorcillo of Dolores was Don Rosalio Eduarte. The municipality covers a land area of 47.45 square kilometres (18.32 sq mi), which constitutes 1.14% of Abra’s total area of 4,165.25 square kilometres (1,608.21 sq mi), and is located at 17°39′N 120°43′E (17.65°N 120.71°E). It is situated 17.42 kilometres (10.82 mi) from the provincial capital Bangued and 423.27 kilometres (263.01 mi) from Manila. Dolores is politically subdivided into 15 barangays, each consisting of puroks and some having sitios. The population density is 250 inhabitants per square kilometre (650/sq mi). The municipality belongs to the lone congressional district of Abra and is governed by a mayor, who serves as the local chief executive, and a municipal council, which functions as the legislative body, in accordance with the Local Government Code. These officials are elected directly by the people every three years. The Dolores Schools District Office oversees all educational institutions within the municipality, managing and operating both public and private schools from primary to secondary levels.
